'''''Erica erigena''''', the '''Irish heath''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17}}</ref> is a European [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Ericaceae.

==Description==
It is a compact [[evergreen]] [[shrub]] growing to {{convert|75|cm|0|abbr=off}}, with somewhat brittle foliage and deep pink honey-scented flowers in winter and spring.<ref name="RHSAZ">{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Great plant picks - ''Erica erigena''|url=http://www.greatplantpicks.org/plantlists/view/563|accessdate=19 June 2013}}</ref> The leaves are 4-whorled, measuring {{Convert|5-8|mm|frac=8}} in length and turning dark green at maturity.<ref>Poland J, Clement EJ. 2020. ''The Vegetative Key to the British Flora''. Second Edition. John Poland, Southampton {{ISBN|978-0-9560-1442-9}}</ref>

Originally known as ''Erica mediterranea'', the species was renamed in 1969 by [[Robert Ross (botanist)|R. Ross]]. The species name ''erigena'' comes from [[Ériu|Erin of Ireland]] as "one applicable to something of Irish origin". ''E. mediterranea'' is now more commonly used to refer to ''[[Erica carnea|E. carnea]]''.<ref name=Proudley>{{cite book |author1=Brian Proudley |author2=Valerie Proudley |title=Heathers in Colour |date=1989 |publisher=Blandford Press |isbn=0713714204 |page=140 |edition=2nd |quote=}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
It is [[Native species|native]] to Ireland, southwestern France, Spain, Portugal and Tangier. Its appearance in the far west of Ireland, separated from the main Mediterranean populations, suggests a [[wikt:garden escape|garden escape]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Foss|first=Peter J.|last2=Doyle|first2=Gerard J.|title=The history of Erica erigena R. Ross, an Irish plant with a disjunct European distribution|journal=Journal of Quaternary Science|volume=5|pages=1–16|doi=10.1002/jqs.3390050102|year=1990}}</ref> It prefers cliffs and heathland.
==Cultivation==
In cultivation, it is often seen as [[groundcover]] amongst dwarf [[pinophyta|conifers]].  Like others of its kind, it is a [[calcifuge]], preferring an open sunny site with well-drained acid soil. Numerous [[cultivars]] have been developed for garden use, of which the following have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]]:<ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 33 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 6 February 2018}}</ref> 
*''Erica erigena'' 'Irish Dusk'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Erica erigena'' 'Irish Dusk'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/91666/Erica-erigena-Irish-Dusk/Details | accessdate = 7 June 2020}}</ref> 
*''Erica erigena'' f. ''alba'' 'W.T. Rackliff'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Erica erigena'' f. ''alba'' 'W.T. Rackliff'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/75195/Erica-erigena-f-alba-W-T-Rackliff/Details | accessdate = 7 June 2020}}</ref> (white-flowered)
